rationale: Issue #889 ("grouped field declaration keeps only the first name") is one surface of a class: a declaration that names N names declares N symbols, and a declaration that names NO name still declares a FIELD when it is embedded. Before this fixture the lane published, on one struct, `A` and silently dropped `B`/`C` of `A, B, C int`, published NOTHING for the embedded fields `Inner` and `*Pair[int, string]`, and published the blank padding field `_ bool` as a symbol named `_` (the GO5 rule the var/const path already applied). Every name asserted below is the Go language contract, not the analyzer's output: the spec states that `A, B, C int` declares three fields, that "the unqualified type name acts as the field name" for an embedded field (so `Inner` declares a field `Inner`), and that `_` is not a declaration. The leaf rule for the embedded `*Pair[int, string]` is the same one the analyzer's embedded-INTERFACE path already used (its member symbol is `Closer` for `io.Closer`), which is also why the embedding edge (`mixes_in`, the struct half) must spell the embedded type by LEAF (`Pair`) and not by raw source text (`Pair[int, string]`). The draft of this fixture did its job before the expectation was written: running it caught a first attempt at the embedded rule that read the blank field `_ bool` as "an embedded field named bool" — recorded here because the `_`/embedded distinction is exactly what the two forbid entries below pin.
